preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services IRS notice CP207, Q2 2026 Form 941
preview.body:
Hi,

We received the attached IRS notice CP207 on October 29 for our Q2 2026 Form 941. It proposes a deposit penalty of $1,348.09 and says our return showed monthly liabilities instead of a Schedule B. Please work out whether the penalty is right and draft our reply. The notice is dated October 26, so we have 45 days.

As far as I know, Northline Payroll Services deposits every regular payroll on time through EFTPS; the EFTPS history and the return as filed are attached, and the payroll by payday, our employer details and the IRS account history are in the folder.

Two things you should know:

- The May 21 off-cycle bonus run was not released for tax filing in the provider portal, so its deposit did not go out. I caught it in the June reconciliation and made the deposit myself on June 5.
- Northline Payroll Services confirmed that the Q3 return they filed on October 30 used the same monthly setting on line 16, with no Schedule B.

Thanks,
Morgan Lee
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC

passages.q: What are the IRS's First Time Abate criteria for a deposit penalty, and which comes first, the waiver or reasonable cause?
passages.a: IRS provides administrative relief from the following penalties ... Failure to Deposit (FTD) penalty under IRC 6656. ... When determining if FTA criteria are met, the criteria below applies to the same MFT as the penalized MFT ... A total of four or more FTD penalty waiver codes are present in the taxpayer's three-year penalty history. ... Penalty relief under administrative waivers, including FTA, is to be considered and applied before reasonable cause. ... Do not provide relief under the FTA waiver if there is clear and convincing evidence that the taxpayer did in fact comply.

passages.q: How exactly does the IRS average a semiweekly depositor's monthly liabilities?
passages.a: Monthly liability schedule provided- semi-weekly depositors: Divide each month's tax liability by 4. Assign the resulting tax liabilities to the first four Wednesdays of each month. ... Master File computes a proposed penalty by averaging the tax and generates a CP 207 or CP 207L notice (proposed averaged penalty) ... If the taxpayer provides a completed ROFTL schedule: compute the penalty based on the taxpayer's figures.

sources.title: Administrative penalty relief (First Time Abate and Automatic Exemption from Penalty)

passages.q: Is First Time Abate available for a Q2 2026 deposit penalty, and does HANGS's history qualify?
passages.a: AEP begins summer 2026. Under AEP, if you file or pay late in the current year but have timely filed returns and paid tax due for the three prior years (or 12 consecutive quarters for quarterly filers), you won't be assessed a penalty. ... 2025 tax year returns, and subsequent 2026 quarterly returns, and subsequent ... The same return type, as the original return, was timely filed for the prior three years (or 12 consecutive quarters), and either no penalty (except the estimated tax penalty) was assessed or a penalty was assessed, but later abated for reasonable cause or IRS error ... The IRS did not waive the failure to deposit penalty four or more times during the prior three years (or 12

passages.q: What does notice CP207 ask for, and by when?
passages.a: We are notifying you that your deposit schedule, the record of federal tax liability (ROFTL), contains missing or incorrect information. ... Complete a new ROFTL and mail to the address at the top of your notice within 45 days of the date on your notice. ... If you're on a semi-weekly schedule, list the tax liability amount for each pay date. Report only liabilities, not your deposits.

passages.q: What happens without a reply, and where does a reasonable-cause statement go?
passages.a: We'll figure a penalty by averaging the total tax liability across the tax period. We'll apply your deposits to the average liabilities in the order we receive them. ... We can't consider requests to remove deposit penalties unless we have a correct ROFTL. If you believe you had reasonable cause for making a deposit late, include a statement signed under penalty of perjury with your reply.

passages.q: Are days late counted in business days or calendar days?
passages.a: We calculate the amount of the Failure to Deposit Penalty based on the number of calendar days your deposit is late, starting from its due date. The penalty amounts don't add up.

Use Form 843 to claim a refund or request an abatement of certain taxes, penalties, additions to tax, interest, and fees. ... If you are requesting a refund or an abatement of an assessed penalty, enter the applicable Internal Revenue Code section. ... Forms 843 filed by corporations must be signed by a corporate officer authorized to sign ... If your authorized representative files Form 843, the original or copy of Form 2848, Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative, must be attached.

passages.q: Which lookback period applies for 2026, and what must a semiweekly depositor file with Form 941?
passages.a: For 2026, the lookback period begins July 1, 2024, and ends June 30, 2025. ... If you reported more than $50,000 of taxes for the lookback period, you're a semiweekly schedule depositor. Check the third box on line 16. You must complete Schedule B (Form 941) and submit it with your Form 941.

passages.q: What goes on the Schedule B sent with the reply?
passages.a: On Schedule B, list your tax liability for each day. Your tax liability is based on the dates wages were paid. ... Don't use Schedule B to show federal tax deposits. ... If you have been assessed a failure-to-deposit (FTD) penalty, you may be able to file an amended Schedule B. ... The IRS will refigure the penalty and notify you of any change in the penalty.

passages.q: Was HANGS a monthly or a semiweekly schedule depositor in 2026?
passages.a: If you're a Form 941 filer, your deposit schedule for a calendar year is determined from the total taxes reported on Forms 941, line 12, in a 4-quarter lookback period. ... If you reported $50,000 or less of taxes for the lookback period, you're a monthly schedule depositor; if you reported more than $50,000, you're a semiweekly schedule depositor. Table 1. Lookback Period for Calendar Year 2026: July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025.

passages.q: When was each Q2 deposit due?
passages.a: Under the semiweekly deposit schedule, deposit employment taxes for payments made on Wednesday, Thursday, and/or Friday by the following Wednesday. ... If any of the 3 weekdays after the end of a semiweekly period is a legal holiday, you'll have an additional day for each day that is a legal holiday to make the required deposit. ... May 25-Memorial Day

passages.q: Why did the IRS propose an averaged penalty?
passages.a: The IRS may also assess an "averaged" FTD penalty of 2% to 10% if you're a semiweekly schedule depositor and your tax liability shown on Form 941, line 12 ... equaled or exceeded $2,500 and you: Completed Form 941, line 16, instead of Schedule B (Form 941) ... Then we apply your deposits and payments to the averaged liabilities in the date order we received your deposits.

passages.q: Would the May 21 deposit qualify for reasonable cause if administrative relief is refused?
passages.a: Reasonable cause is determined on a case-by-case basis considering all the facts and circumstances of your situation. ... For businesses, the reasons apply to the person with authority to submit the return, deposit, or tax. ... Reliance on a tax professional. You're generally responsible for complying with tax law even if someone else handles your taxes. ... Mistakes and oversights. You're responsible for making sure your tax returns, payments and deposits are correct and on time. In certain cases, reasonable cause may apply to a mistake if additional facts and circumstances show that you tried to comply with tax law.

passages.q: What does the law charge for a late deposit, and what excuses it?
passages.a: Unless it is shown that such failure is due to reasonable cause and not due to willful neglect, there shall be imposed upon such person a penalty equal to the applicable percentage of the amount of the underpayment. ... (i) 2 percent if the failure is for not more than 5 days, (ii) 5 percent if the failure is for more than 5 days but not more than 15 days, and (iii) 10 percent if the failure is for more than 15 days.
